newsitem.title: USA: IPO PRICING - Westfield Financial at $15, below range.
newsitem.headline: IPO PRICING - Westfield Financial at $15, below range.

text.p: Shares of Westfield America Inc, the U.S. real estate investment trust (REIT) run by property mogul Frank Lowy, the third-richest man in Australia, priced lower than expected late on Thursday.
The Los Angeles based REIT invests in malls in the United States. Shares priced at $15, below its estimated pricing range of $16 to $17.50 a share, according to lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.

The IPO comes amid stirring popularity for REITs, which were once seen as dull investments with sluggish growth prospects. To keep their special U.S. tax status, REITs must pay out 95 percent of their taxable income to shareholders. With such high payouts, REITs offer can offer a high-income cushion in a market downturn.

For the past year, REIT returns including dividends beat the Standard & Poor's 500 Index with a 29.3 percent gain compared to the S&P's 25.13 percent, according to NAREIT, a Washington-based industry organization.

The bargain price could give the stock some much-needed room to rise in the aftermarket. IPO analysts had said they did not expect shares to rise much above their IPO price at their debut, based on the $16 to $17.50 pricing range, after a critical newspaper report published last week.

The report quoted several REIT experts as saying they did not like Westfield's outside advisory structure. Under that arrangement, a separate outside adviser with different ownership will manage the company.

Westfield will offer 18.0 million shares, raising gross proceeds of about $270 million. Co-underwriters of the deal are Furman Selz, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, Prudential Securities, Smith Barney, and BT Securities.
